ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

fullPassage:
Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and challenges his dad to a match.

Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.

Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect."

When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.

His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough. "No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway." In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.

Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway.

An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder.

The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of improving his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!

You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!

Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties.

The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.

Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.

questions.passage: The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with (A) and courage. Or he could (B) new and challenging experiences and choose an (C), familiar path.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 소년은 인내심(endurance)과 용기로 어려움에 맞서거나, 새로운 경험을 피하고(avoid), 쉬운(easy) 익숙한 길을 택할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② endurance — avoid — easy: 원문 일치
❌ ① reject: avoid 대신 reject는 문맥상 어색
❌ ③ hard: easy의 반의어
❌ ④ avoidance: 명사형으로 동사 자리에 부적절
det.tip: endurance(인내심), avoid(피하다) ↔ embrace(받아들이다), easy ↔ hard

questions.passage: He sets the paddle on the table, saying, 'I have had enough,' and leaves for his room. His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some (A) in his elbow. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion, saying, 'He's going to be (B) than me anyway.' In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than (C).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 팔꿈치의 통증(pain), 오빠가 자신보다 더 잘할(better) 것이라는 체념, 도전을 장애물(obstacles)로만 보는 회피형 사고가 드러난다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① pain — better — obstacles: 원문 일치
❌ ② worse: better의 반의어
❌ ③ comfort: pain의 반의어
❌ ④ rewards: obstacles의 반의어
det.tip: pain ↔ comfort, better ↔ worse, obstacles(장애물) ↔ opportunities(기회)

questions.passage: Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be (A) to germs to build immunity, you must experience (B) to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being (C): you experience, you feel, you fail, you hurt, you fall. But you keep going.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 세균에 노출되어야(exposed) 면역이 생기듯, 어려움(difficulties)을 겪어야 회복탄력성이 생기며, 이는 감정 없음(emotionless)이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ exposed — difficulties — emotionless: 원문 일치
❌ ① emotional: emotionless의 반의어
❌ ② immune: exposed의 반의어
❌ ④ pleasures: difficulties의 반의어
det.tip: be exposed to ↔ be immune to, difficulties ↔ pleasures, emotionless ↔ emotional

questions.passage: His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some ①<u>pain</u> in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the ②<u>challenge</u>. When his mom ③<u>suggests</u> playing against his older brother, he ④<u>accepts</u> her suggestion because his brother is very tough. 'No, thanks,' sighs the boy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 소년은 엄마의 제안을 거절(turns down)한다. ④ accepts(수락하다)는 문맥상 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ accepts(수락하다): 원문은 'turns down(거절하다)' → 부적절
✅ ① pain: 팔꿈치 통증 → 적절
✅ ② challenge: 'taking up the challenge' → 적절
✅ ③ suggests: 제안하다 → 적절
det.tip: turn down = reject(거절) ↔ accept(수락) — 핵심 반의어

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His ①<u>tale</u> shows how an ②<u>ordinary</u> boy developed his ③<u>indifference</u> for table tennis and eventually became the national ④<u>champion</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 소년이 탁구에 대한 열정(passion)을 키워 챔피언이 됐다. ③ indifference(무관심)는 passion의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ indifference(무관심): 원문은 'passion(열정)' → 부적절
✅ ① tale: 이야기 → 적절
✅ ② ordinary: 평범한 → 적절
✅ ④ champion: 챔피언 → 적절
det.tip: passion(열정) ↔ indifference(무관심) — 핵심 반의어

questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem ①<u>fun</u> and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of ②<u>comforts</u>, both big and small. So why can some people ③<u>handle</u> tough times and become ④<u>stronger</u> while others remain unchanged and helpless?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 실제 십대의 삶은 자신만의 도전(challenges)을 가져온다. ② comforts(편안함)는 challenges의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ② comforts(편안함): 원문은 'challenges(도전)' → 부적절
✅ ① fun: 재미있는 → 소셜 미디어 묘사에 적절
✅ ③ handle: 감당하다 → 적절
✅ ④ stronger: 더 강해지다 → 적절
det.tip: challenges(도전/어려움) ↔ comforts(편안함)

questions.passage: He sets the paddle on the table, saying, 'I have had enough,' and leaves for his room. His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than __________, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 회피형 소년에게 도전은 장애물(obstacles)에 불과하며, 피하는 것이 최선이라 믿는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① obstacles(장애물): 원문 일치, 회피 심리와 일관성
❌ ② opportunities: 기회 → 성장형 사고, 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ rewards: 보상 → 회피 이유가 되지 않음
❌ ④ achievements: 성취 → 피할 이유가 없음
det.tip: obstacle = barrier = hurdle(장애물) ↔ opportunity(기회)

questions.passage: He participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his __________ to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 결승전에서 소년의 상대(opponent)가 능숙하고 영리하지만, 소년은 열심히 경기한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ opponent(상대/적수): 1:1 경기 상대 → 원문 일치
❌ ① teammate: 같은 팀 → 경기 상대가 아님
❌ ② coach: 코치 → 경기 상대가 아님
❌ ④ audience: 관객 → 경기 참여자가 아님
det.tip: opponent = rival = adversary(상대방) — 경기 문맥 필수 어휘

questions.passage: So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in __________—the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그 답은 회복탄력성(resilience)에 있다 — 도전적 경험에 적응하는 능력.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ resilience: 이어지는 정의 'ability to adapt to challenging experiences'와 일치
❌ ① endurance: 인내심 → 적응 능력과 다름
❌ ② persistence: 끈기 → 정의 표현과 불일치
❌ ③ confidence: 자신감 → 문맥상 부적절
det.tip: resilience = the ability to adapt to challenging experiences — 정의 문장 암기

questions.passage: Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and <u>courage</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 courage의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 소년은 용기(courage)를 갖고 어려움에 맞설 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② bravery(용감함): courage의 정확한 동의어
❌ ① patience: 인내심 → endurance에 더 가까움
❌ ③ wisdom: 지혜 → 다른 의미
❌ ④ kindness: 친절 → 다른 의미
det.tip: courage = bravery = valor = boldness — 용기 동의어 세트

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his <u>passion</u> for table tennis and eventually became the national champion.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 passion의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 소년이 탁구에 가진 열정(passion)이 그를 국가 챔피언으로 이끌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ enthusiasm(열의): passion의 동의어
❌ ① talent: 재능 → 타고난 능력
❌ ② strategy: 전략 → 다른 의미
❌ ③ ambition: 야망 → 유사하나 passion의 가장 정확한 동의어는 아님
det.tip: passion = enthusiasm = zeal = ardor — 열정 동의어 세트

questions.passage: Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to <u>enhance</u> your resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 enhance의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 회복탄력성을 강화하는(enhance) 데는 시간과 노력이 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① strengthen(강화하다): enhance의 동의어
❌ ② weaken: 약화시키다 → 반의어
❌ ③ measure: 측정하다 → 다른 의미
❌ ④ ignore: 무시하다 → 다른 의미
det.tip: enhance = strengthen = boost = improve ↔ weaken(약화시키다)

questions.passage: The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he <u>participates</u> in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 participates의 의미와 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: 소년은 전국 챔피언십에 참가한다(participates). 의미가 가장 먼 것은 ③ withdraws from(철수하다/빠지다).
det.analysis:
❌ ③ withdraws from(~에서 물러나다): participates의 반의어 → 가장 먼 의미
✅ ① takes part in: 참여하다 → 동의어
✅ ② joins: 참가하다 → 동의어
✅ ④ engages in: 참여하다 → 동의어
det.tip: participate = take part in = engage in ↔ withdraw from(철수하다)

questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. The good news is that humans can <u>recover</u> from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 recover의 의미와 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: 인간은 압박과 고난에서 회복할(recover) 수 있다. 의미가 가장 먼 것은 ② succumb to(굴복하다).
det.analysis:
❌ ② succumb to(~에 굴복하다): recover의 반의어 → 가장 먼 의미
✅ ① bounce back: 회복하다 → 동의어
✅ ③ heal from: ~에서 회복하다 → 동의어
✅ ④ overcome: 극복하다 → 유사 의미
det.tip: recover = bounce back = recuperate ↔ succumb to = give in to

questions.passage: He practices <u>hard</u> after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 hard의 의미가 나머지 셋과 다른 것은?

det.korean: ①③④의 hard는 '열심히(부사)'이고, ②의 hard는 'It is hard to...' 구조에서 '어려운(형용사)'으로 사용됐다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② hard(어려운, 형용사): 'It is hard to+동사원형' 구조
✅ ① hard(열심히, 부사): plays hard
✅ ③ hard(열심히, 부사): practices hard
✅ ④ hard(열심히, 부사): trained hard
det.tip: hard 부사: 열심히 (work/play/train hard) vs 형용사: 어려운 (It is hard to do)

ch: He plays <u>hard</u> and never gives up during the match.
It is <u>hard</u> to recover quickly from such a challenging experience.
She practices <u>hard</u> every morning to improve her game.
He trained <u>hard</u> for months to join the regional team.

questions.passage: The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.
questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the ability to recover quickly from difficulties and adapt to challenging experiences"

det.korean: 어려운 상황에서 빠르게 회복하여 도전적 경험에 적응하는 능력 → resilience(회복탄력성)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ resilience: 영영 정의와 정확히 일치
❌ ① endurance: 인내심 — 버티는 능력, 회복과 다름
❌ ② ambition: 야망 — 목표를 이루려는 욕망
❌ ④ immunity: 면역 — 질병에 저항하는 능력
det.tip: resilience 정의 3요소: recover + adapt + challenging experiences

questions.passage: He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!
questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a great victory or achievement; the feeling of joy after succeeding"

det.korean: 위대한 승리 또는 성취; 성공 후의 기쁨 → triumph(승리/쾌거)
det.analysis:
✅ ② triumph: 영영 정의와 정확히 일치
❌ ① defeat: 패배 → 반의어
❌ ③ challenge: 도전 → 과정이지 결과가 아님
❌ ④ obstacle: 장애물 → 다른 의미
det.tip: triumph = victory = success ↔ defeat(패배)

questions.passage: When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. He sets the paddle on the table, __________ (say), 'I have had enough,' and leaves for his room.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 분사구문 — 패들을 내려놓으며 동시에 '충분히 했다'고 말하면서(saying)
det.analysis:
say → saying: 동시동작 분사구문
주절 주어(He)와 동일 → 접속사·주어 생략 + 동사 → 현재분사(-ing)
det.tip: 분사구문: 접속사 + 주어 생략 → V-ing (주절과 동시 동작 표현)

questions.passage: The answer lies in resilience—the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties. Think of it like __________ (build) your body's immune system.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 전치사 like 다음 동명사 — 면역 체계를 구축하는 것처럼(building) 생각하라
det.analysis:
build → building: 전치사(like) 다음에는 동명사(-ing)
'Think of A like B': B처럼 A를 생각하다 → like + 동명사
det.tip: 전치사 + 동명사: like/for/of/without + V-ing (전치사 뒤 동사원형 불가)

questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 회복탄력성은 문제를 막아주지 않지만, 맞서고 극복하도록(face and overcome them) 도와준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② face and overcome them: 원문 일치
